Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the post-Tea session. Najmul Hossain Shanto leads his troops out onto the park. It will be the experienced pair of Andy Balbirnie and Paul Stirling at the top of the order for Ireland. Right-arm quick, Ebadot Hossain will kickstart proceedings with the new ball. Balbirnie to face. Three slips and a gully await. Let's go...
... SECOND INNINGS ...

With the end of the Bangladesh innings, Tea has been taken earlier than scheduled. The surface has certainly offered more turn compared to the opening day, but it has not been sharp, and with the pitch on the slower side, the turn has been manageable for the batters. In the first Test in Sylhet, it was a case of Irish batters getting starts but failing to convert them into big scores, something they must correct here in Mirpur if they are to challenge the home side. Do join us back after the break for the start of the Irish reply.

Thanks to some lower-order hitting from Ebadot Hossain, the home side were able to push their total up to 476. A substantial score without a doubt, though they would feel they could have gotten even more. For Ireland, Andy McBrine finished with a six-wicket haul, but surprisingly bowled only five overs in the first session today and was brought back into the attack nearly 90 minutes into the second. That was puzzling unless he is carrying some sort of niggle.

Bangladesh end up with 476 on the board. Ireland will feel they have limited the damage to some extent, considering the hosts were cruising at 433/5 before losing their last five wickets for 43. That said, the real challenge lies ahead when they come out to bat. After losing the toss, Ireland had their tails up early when they reduced Bangladesh to 95/3 in the morning. But what followed was a trio of 100-plus stands that firmly put the hosts on top, with Mushfiqur Rahim and Litton Das both going on to reach their respective hundreds.

Ireland have to get their think-tank together as Bangladesh are running away with a massive first innings total. The pitch is still pretty comfortable to bat on, with the odd ones bouncing or staying low to keep the batters guessing. However, Ireland need more than the odd balls to remain in the game. The spinners dominated the session but without much to offer. Ireland will look to break this partnership in the next session, while Bangladesh will try and breach the 500-mark in the next session or so. Stay tuned.

A dominating start to the game and to Day 2 for the hosts as well. They are currently in a comfortable position. Bangladesh added 95 runs to the overnight total while losing just one wicket of the maestro Mushfiqur Rahim. All eyes were on the keeper-batter who was stranded on 99 in his 100th Test match. Day 2 began with several milestones. Mushfiqur Rahim's13th Test century, Litton Das' 19th fifty in Test and the pair adding 100 runs together. Rahim fell right after his century but that didn't stop Bangladesh from pouring in more runs as Das found an able partner in Mehidy Hasan Miraz, who helped Bangladesh stay on track with a 77-run unbeaten stand.
Serves a googly, full and around off, Mehidy Hasan Miraz reaches out in front to smother the spin. That will be LUNCH on Day 2!

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set. Another pleasant morning in Mirpur, and the crowd has come in anticipation of a Mushfiqur Rahim hundred. A big cheer goes around as Rahim walks out alongside Litton Das. Ireland are starting with spin in the form of Matthew Humphreys. Mushfiqur to face. A slip and a gully in place. Here we go!

PITCH REPORT - Isabella Joyce says the conditions could not be better for cricket today, and Ireland will need to be at their best. Believes that Andy McBrine kept things simple on Day 1, varying his lengths nicely and got rewards for his discipline. Mentions that there is a bit of grass covering on the surface, but it is loose, resulting in a bit of grip and slow turn. She adds that the pitch feels compact rather than hard, which is contributing to the low bounce. Adds that cracks have already started to form and could widen as the game goes on, making batting progressively tougher.

Andy McBrine is up next. He says it is nice to be back in Mirpur, a venue where he had a bit of success in 2023. Feels the team stuck to their plans well on Day 1 and showed good discipline throughout. States that he is not too sure how Mushfiqur Rahim would have slept on 99 overnight, but playing 100 Tests show the longevity and class Rahim has had over the years. McBrine adds that the wicket played pretty well on the opening day and the key now is to assess quickly and make the most of the conditions this morning.

Mominul Haque is up for a quick chat. He starts by saying on Mushfiqur Rahim that it takes a lot of effort to play for the country for the past 20 years and is incredible. Tells that it might take one episode to describe about Rahim. Shares that Rahim makes things very easy as he reads the game really well and also the situation. Reckons that the board celebrated Mushfiqur's 100th Test in a grand way and that will inspire many youngsters to keep their dream alive to play for Bangladesh.

As for Ireland, their bowling was fairly disciplined on a surface that offered very little assistance on the opening day. However, they put down three chances, two off Mominul and one off Mushfiqur, and had any of those been converted, the complexion of the day could have been very different. They will need to put that behind them and make the second new ball, which is 10 overs old, really count this morning. Stay tuned as the first ball on Day 2 is not far away.

Having opted to bat first, Bangladesh lost three wickets in the morning session before Mominul Haque, Mushfiqur Rahim and Litton Das dug deep to keep the Irish bowlers at bay. It must have been an anxious night for Mushfiqur, unbeaten on 99 in his 100th Test, and the fans will turn up hoping to see him reach three figures and push on. Ideally, the hosts will want to bat once and bat big.

Hello and a warm welcome, everyone, to Day 2 of the second and final Test here in Mirpur. Yesterday was a good day at the office for the hosts, and it is now about building on the platform they have laid. The beauty of Test cricket is that it always offers a chance to fight back, and Ireland will need a meaningful response today or risk falling too far behind.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

Frustrations rose in the Irish camp as they saw the Rahim-Das alliance growing stronger over after over. Two of the most experienced batters in this Bangladeshi camp ensured that there were no further hiccups as the day drew to a close. As expected, we saw a barrage of spin from Ireland to exploit the slowish nature of the wicket. Of a total of 90 overs bowled in the day, 76 were delivered by the spinners. The same can be expected for the second day as well and as the game goes on. Ireland need wickets and need to come afresh on the second day to challenge the hosts with renewed determination whereas Bangladesh would bank on this particular partnership to play the long haul. We will be back for Day 2 as it begins on Thursday, 20th November with the first ball scheduled to be bowled at 3.30 am GMT. Until then, stay safe. Ta-ta!

McBrine struck immediately after being reintroduced, ending Mominul Haque's stay early in the final session. But that only brought Litton Das to the crease, who linked up with Mushfiqur Rahim for yet another rock-solid stand. Rahim brought up his fifty, and Ireland's frustration grew. And that was Ireland's day in a nutshell. The older ball went soft, lost its bite, and Ireland lost their edge. Partnerships kept blooming in the middle, with Rahim pulling the strings like a maestro. Ireland huffed, toiled really hard, but got very little in return.

Bangladesh bossed the afternoon session, adding 92 runs without loss and making Ireland look toothless. Mominul Haque eased to his fifty while Mushfiqur Rahim, in his 100th Test, played the perfect foil. They played smart cricket - rotating strike, milking gaps, and cashing in when the bowlers erred. Three catches were spilled, two of Mominul, and later, Rahim was also offered a reprieve as they stretched their stand to triple figures. Had either of the chances stuck, the session could have flipped. Instead, they watched Bangladesh cruise. The surprising part? McBrine, their best spinner, was mysteriously sidelined for a part-timer in Tector. Even with grip and turn on offer, Ireland couldn't capitalize much.

It has been a very slow and absorbing opening day of this second and final Test match. So let's rewind a bit and take a sneak peek. Bangladesh won the toss and elected to bat first. They blazed to 52 in the first hour, with Shadman Islam attacking freely as Ireland's pacers sprayed it around and wasted early movement. Skipper Andy Balbirnie quickly turned to spin, and Andy McBrine - the only bowler showing real discipline - struck just before the hydration break to end the opening stand. Spin in tandem from McBrine and Humphreys then strangled the scoring with stump-to-stump lines and subtle turn. The pressure told as Mahmudul Hasan Joy threw his wicket away attacking McBrine, who soon claimed the Bangladeshi captain with a beauty to cap Ireland's fightback in the first session.

Okay, hang on! Are we getting another over? Umpire Sam Nogajski waits for the confirmation. Nope. STUMPS are called as we have gone past the allotted time. Exactly 90 overs completed. A very good day of cricket. Take a bow, Mushfiqur Rahim! He walks back to the dugout and gets a guard of honour from his teammates. He ends his day on a nervous 99, but hasn't been remotely nervous at all throughout the day. We wonder who scripts moments like these? Overall, a good job from the hosts as they hold an upper hand in the contest. A rather frustrating day from Ireland's perspective as they were made to toil hard. They were good in patches, especially whenever Andy McBrine came to bowl, but they would definitely admit that they were a bit sloppy in the field.

... DAY 1, THIRD SESSION ...

The surface has not changed much from how it played at the start of the day, but with the sun beating down, it remains to be seen whether it begins to offer more spin in the third session. From Bangladesh's perspective, the afternoon was about steady accumulation, but with the bowlers tiring towards the end of the day, it will be interesting to see if the tempo changes after the break. As for Ireland, it will be about being disciplined and targeting the stumps as much as they can. Join us back at 8.30 am GMT for the third and final session of the day. Cheers!

With McBrine given a breather, debutant leg-spinner Gavin Hoey stepped in seamlessly and kept probing away. Mominul Haque and Mushfiqur Rahim were content to bide their time against the spinners and avoided taking undue risks. The pair had their share of luck as well, with Mominul dropped on 23 and 49, while Rahim was given a reprieve on 22. 46 runs came in the 17 overs of the first hour, and 46 more were scored in the next hour across 14 overs.

SESSION SUMMARY - 92 runs in 31 overs. A successful session for Bangladesh. Having lost three wickets in the morning, the hosts would have ideally aimed to get through this session without losing another and they have done exactly that. Ireland toiled away without any success, but had the chances been converted, they might have been in a very different position heading into the final session. Andy McBrine picked up where he left off before the break with his discipline. After three overs of pace, Andy Balbirnie turned to spin from both ends, and that remained the theme of the attack for the rest of the session.
Gavin drops it short and gets it to turn across the batter. Mushfiqur Rahim gets on the back foot and steers it through cover-point for a single. And that will be TEA on Day 1!

Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the post-Lunch session. The over rate in the first session was pretty good as maximum overs were bowled by spinners. Expect more or less the same in this afternoon phase as well. The umpires and players punctually make their way out to the center. Mushfiqur Rahim and Mominul Haque walk out to resume their batting. ... DAY 1, SECOND SESSION ...

Bangladesh had to dial it back a bit after their strong start against pace. The surface didn’t have any real tricks up its sleeve. Just a touch of hold and turn to keep batters honest. But the template of bowling stump-to-stump from both spinners proved to be effective in restricting easy run flow. The patience finally wore out as Mahmudul Hasan Joy threw his wicket away trying to attack McBrine's spin, who soon capped off the session by outfoxing the Bangladeshi skipper off a beauty. Coming into the post-Lunch session, the hosts will expect some longevity through Mushfiqur Rahim, while the tourists will aim to get rid of him as quickly as possible to dent through the middle order. Join us back as play resumes at 6.10 am GMT.

The hosts clearly owned the early exchanges, scoring 52 in the first hour itself. With the seamers offering little, Balbirinie quickly turned to spin. Andy McBrine was the only bowler who showed real discipline in that opening hour, and fittingly it was he who finally cracked the stand with Ireland’s first wicket just before the hydration break. Spin came on in tandem, and McBrine and Humphreys ripped through their overs and stitched together a string of dots.

Bangladesh got off the blocks with intent after choosing to bat on a fresh surface. Ireland’s pacers never really hit the right areas, spraying it too short or too full, and whatever little movement was there early went completely unused. Shadman Islam punished anything outside off and picked off boundaries with ease, while Mahmudul Hasan Joy played the steady hand at the other end.

When in the subcontinent, spin is the real king, they say. Well, truly said. Ireland would be the happier of the two sides to head into the sheds for Lunch as they picked up three important wickets, all through the spin of Andy McBrine. The first hour belonged to the hosts though as they scored freely against an inconsistent pace attack. But come the second hour, the trial by spin saw the tourists clawing their way back in the contest.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK! Ireland have struck right at the stroke of the hour. Andy McBrine, who has been the most disciplined of the Irish bowlers so far, is rewarded for his persistence, and his wicket is exactly what the visitors needed. His approach provides a blueprint for the rest of the attack, given that there hasn’t been much assistance from the surface in the opening exchanges. Earlier on, the Irish pacers did not quite make the most of the movement that was briefly on offer, struggling with their consistency, and the two Bangladeshi openers were quick to capitalise whenever the bowlers strayed in line or length. A steady start for Bangladesh despite the loss of Shadman Islam, and now it is about building on this platform. Mominul Haque joins Mahmudul Hasan Joy out in the middle.

OUT! LBW! Andy McBrine breaks the frustrating opening partnership with a lovely delivery. On a fractionally fuller length and this one slides on with the arm. Shadman Islam is forced to play at that due to the angle and tries to push it straight back, but the ball keeps drifting into the batter. The ball beats the inside edge and thuds the front pad. A massive appeal goes on for LBW, but the umpire is unmoved. And this time, Andy Balbirnie does opt for a review to challenge the on-field decision, as this looked straight in real time. Nothing on UltraEdge and the Ball Tracking shows the ball is projected to crash into the leg stump. Three reds and he is gone. The on-field decision is reversed. A good review from Ireland. Shadman Islam departs after a very positive start. 35 off 44 deliveries for him, and Bangladesh are 52/1.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to get going. It is a bright and sunny morning in Mirpur. The crowd is sparse for now, but as word spreads that Bangladesh are batting first and that Mushfiqur Rahim could be out in the middle today, more fans are certain to make their way in. Mahmudul Hasan Joy and Shadman Islam are the two openers for Bangladesh. Ireland are starting with pace in the form of Jordan Neill. Mahmudul to face. Three slips and a gully in place. Here we go!

Mushfiqur Rahim is up for a quick chat. He first thanks the Almighty and his family for being a constant support. Also mentions the way his coaches and friends have been right with him throughout. Also thanks the Irish team for acknowledging his journey. Is hopeful that they will have a great Test match.

The captain of Bangladesh, Najmul Hossain Shanto, congratulates Rahim on his 100th Test appearance. He says Rahim always inspired him and others in the team with the way he put his hard work on and off the field. Mentions that he always puts his team first and thinks about the betterment of the team. He is hopeful that Rahim will always continue to deliver like this for the Bangladeshi cricket team.

Before we get underway, the Bangladesh Cricket Board will felicitate Mushfiqur Rahim on the occasion of his 100th Test. Rahim has his family present with him for this special moment. Former Bangladesh cricketer Habibul Bashar steps forward to present a special cap to Mushfiqur Rahim. Interestingly, it was Bashar, the captain then, who had also handed Rahim his maiden Test cap back in 2005. Akram Khan, Bangladesh’s Test Cap Number 1, joins in the felicitation and presents Mushfiqur with a special Test cap casquet. Next up, Bashar and current skipper Najmul Hossain Shanto present Rahim with a framed jersey signed by all members of the squad.

Ireland (Playing XI) - Paul Stirling, Andy Balbirnie (C), Cade Carmichael, Harry Tector, Curtis Campher, Lorcan Tucker (WK), Stephen Doheny (On debut) (In for Barry McCarthy), Andy McBrine, Jordan Neill, Gavin Hoey (On debut) (In for Craig Young), Matthew Humphreys.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Shadman Islam, Mahmudul Hasan Joy, Mominul Haque, Najmul Hossain Shanto (C), Mushfiqur Rahim, Litton Das (WK), Mehidy Hasan Miraz, Taijul Islam, Ebadot Hossain (In for Hasan Mahmud), Hasan Murad, Khaled Ahmed (In for Nahid Rana).
TOSS - Bangladesh have won the toss and they will BAT first.

Bangladesh have lost their previous two Tests at this venue, one against South Africa and the other against New Zealand, and that glimmer of history will give Ireland a sliver of belief. But they will have to punch well above their weight to turn that hope into something meaningful. Stick around for the toss and team news.

As for Ireland, they showed flashes of promise with the bat in Sylhet, with several players getting starts but failing to convert them into the substantial scores needed to challenge the hosts. That is certainly something Andy Balbirnie would have addressed in the lead-up to this Test. On the bowling front, left-arm spinner Matthew Humphreys impressed in just his fourth Test, while the experienced Andy McBrine had a quiet outing and will be keen to make amends in conditions better suited to his craft.

Starting with Bangladesh, the major talking point heading into this Test is the milestone of Mushfiqur Rahim, who is all set to become the first Bangladeshi to play 100 Tests. The veteran will be eager to mark the occasion with a three-figure score, something that has eluded him at home for more than a year. With the ball, it was a collective effort in Sylhet across both innings, and their spin attack will relish the far more spin-friendly conditions anticipated in Mirpur.

Hello, one and all! From Sylhet, we have moved to Mirpur for the second and final Test of the series between Bangladesh and Ireland. The hosts arrive with an unassailable lead after handing the Irish an innings defeat, while Ireland will be desperate to hit back and square the series. It promises to be another stern examination for the visitors, perhaps an even tougher one, with conditions at the Shere Bangla National Stadium expected to offer greater assistance to the spinners.
